title: Reliability initiative cadence: guardrails, telemetry gates, and rollback criteria
creator: Aisha Kline
description: Establish a repeatable monthly cadence and concrete guardrails for reliability initiatives that ties SLI targets, error budget consumption, and telemetry sign-off into rollout/rollback decisions. This ticket captures the MVP workflow, required dashboards, notification thresholds, and the automated/hand-off rules engineering teams will rely on when error budgets approach depletion or SLI regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical playbook (Confluence) exists describing the monthly cadence and the chain of responsibility for each phase (monitoring, triage, mitigation, rollback).
Dashboards with SLI burn and projected error budget runway are available for all services in the Reliability Initiative Hub.
Runbook triggers are encoded as explicit thresholds (e.g., 7-day burn rate > X leads to canary pause; 24h burn > Y triggers rollback).
An automated notification path (PagerDuty + Slack) for guardrail breaches is configured and validated in staging.
A small experiment (2 services) completes a full cadence run and demonstrates automated gating & manual rollback within the target SLO window.
milestones: Design guardrail matrix and thresholds — due 2025-02-10
Build SLI burnback dashboard templates — due 2025-02-28
Implement notification wiring and playbook drafts — due 2025-03-14
Pilot with two product teams and collect feedback — due 2025-03-31
Iterate thresholds and automate canary pause action — due 2025-04-10
success_metrics: Reduction in unexpected production rollbacks by 30% in pilot services over 6 weeks
Average time from guardrail breach detection to mitigation <= 45 minutes in pilot
>90% of incidents triggered by SLI breach include rollback/retry action documented in runbook
Product and infra teams report >70% satisfaction with visibility and decision tooling in post-pilot survey
risks: Overly conservative thresholds cause frequent unnecessary rollbacks impacting availability
Inconsistent SLI definitions across services lead to noisy dashboards and false positives
Notification fatigue if thresholds are mis-tuned during initial rollout
Automation misfires for degraded non-critical paths without proper service labeling
decisions: Adopt 7-day burn rate and 24-hour burn rate as primary gating signals (vs single instant SLI drop).
Pilot will use 'canary pause' (stop new canary traffic) before full rollback for services that support canary routing.
Fallback actions prioritized: canary pause -> scale-up safer variant -> full rollback.
Thresholds will be service-classified (critical/high/standard) with different numeric gates to reduce noisy escalations.
